concerns.text: Task T005c1b_primary implements a conditional skip of the Spec's mandatory FR-001 data source (NOAA/PRISM) based on a deviation document. The Spec does not authorize a 'fallback' to Daymet; it mandates NOAA/PRISM. This task silently relaxes the FR-001 constraint by allowing the pipeline to proceed with a non-compliant data source if the deviation document exists, violating the Spec's single source of truth.

Task T043a hardcodes arbitrary numerical targets (0.95, 0.90, 7) for Success Criteria SC-002, SC-003, and SC-004 which are explicitly marked '[deferred]' in the Spec. The Spec requires these targets to be measured against a '[deferred]' value, implying the value is unknown or to be determined by data. Hardcoding these values in the task creates a false pass/fail condition that contradicts the Spec's requirement to measure against the actual (deferred) target, effectively weakening the acceptance criteria.

Task T053_fallback introduces a mechanism to reduce the shuffle count from the Spec's mandatory 10,000 (FR-005) based on runtime. The Spec and Plan do not contain a ratified protocol for reducing shuffle counts or applying Bonferroni corrections as a substitute for the required 10,000 shuffles. This task silently relaxes the FR-005 constraint, violating the deterministic requirement for 10,000 shuffles unless the Spec is explicitly amended to allow this fallback.

Task T023a_gp treats the Gaussian Process (GP) random effect as a post-hoc enhancement added after the initial GAMM fit (T023a). The Spec (US-2, FR-004) requires the GP to be part of the model fit to account for spatial autocorrelation. Splitting this into a sequential 'enhancement' task risks violating the requirement that the GP be integrated into the model fitting process itself, potentially producing a model that does not meet the Spec's definition of the required GAMM structure.
